Loads one picture that holds several frames laid out left to right, top to bottom, and returns a texture that can show any of them. Choose the frame to show with the frame argument of [EntityTexture](EntityTexture), [BrushTexture](BrushTexture) or [TextureBuffer](TextureBuffer). The flags are the same as for [CreateTexture](CreateTexture).

The frames are the layers of one image on the graphics card, so a texture with 100 frames is one texture to the graphics card, and entities that show different frames of it are drawn together. Like in the original, where every frame is a texture of its own, each frame has its own mip maps (flag 8) and is filtered and wrapped by itself: the coordinates that go past a frame come back at its other side, and linear filtering never shows the frame next to it. A picture that is block compressed (DDS) or holds more than 8 bits per channel stays one sheet instead, in which the filtering and the smaller mip maps do also reach into the neighbouring frames.

`first_frame` is the cell that counts as frame 0, and `frame_count` is how many cells are used from there. A sheet 256 pixels wide with 64 pixel frames has four cells per row, so cell 5 is the second cell of the second row.

**Animated pictures.** With a `frame_width` or `frame_height` of 0, an animated GIF, animated WebP or animated AVIF file loads as its frames: they are stored as frames, [TextureWidth](TextureWidth) and [TextureHeight](TextureHeight) are the size of one frame, [TextureFrames](TextureFrames) is how many there are, and [TextureFrameDelay](TextureFrameDelay) is how long each lasts. `first_frame` and `frame_count` then choose some of the frames (a `frame_count` of 0 is all the rest). The sheet is at most 8192 pixels wide and high; an animation that needs more is not loaded and a warning says so. Memory is 4 bytes per pixel of every frame, so a 512x512 animation of 100 frames takes 100 MB. A file that is not animated loads as before. Animated PNG (APNG) is intentionally not supported and counts as a plain PNG.

```blitzbasic
;media gif textures/loadanimtexture.gif 40 10
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
CameraClsColor camera, 70, 100, 160
light = CreateLight()
RotateEntity light, 40, 30, 0
cube = CreateCube()
PositionEntity cube, 0, 0, 4.2
TurnEntity cube, 20, 30, 0

; Draw a sheet of 4 frames, 64 pixels each, and keep it in a file.
sheet = CreateTexture(256, 64, 1 + 4096)
SetBuffer TextureBuffer(sheet)
ClsColor 0, 0, 0
Cls
For f = 0 To 3
	Color 40 + f * 60, 200 - f * 40, 80
	Rect f * 64 + 4, 4, 56, 56, 1
	Color 255, 255, 255
	Text f * 64 + 32, 32, Str(f), 1, 1
Next
SaveBuffer TextureBuffer(sheet), "wiki_sheet.bmp"
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
FreeTexture sheet

anim = LoadAnimTexture("wiki_sheet.bmp", 1, 64, 64, 0, 4)
For i = 0 To 39
	EntityTexture cube, anim, (i / 10) Mod 4
	TurnEntity cube, 0, 2, 0
	RenderWorld
	Flip
Next
```

![LoadAnimTexture](media/textures/loadanimtexture.gif)
@param file         Picture file that contains all frames.
@param flags        Texture flags, see CreateTexture.
@param frame_width  Width of one frame in pixels.
@param frame_height Height of one frame in pixels.
@param first_frame  Cell of the sheet that is frame 0.
@param frame_count  How many frames the texture has.
@returns A texture handle, or 0 if the file could not be loaded.
@gap JPEG 2000 files do not load, and TIFF files with Deflate or JPEG compression do not, which the original read. WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL and DDS load instead, see [Image formats](Image-Formats).
@gap TextureWidth and TextureHeight report the size of one frame, not of the whole sheet.
